messages:
Ajay: heads up — saw a big drop in prefix cache hit rate after yesterday's fused-attn + quant-profile-v2 rollout.
Leah: how big we talking?
Ajay: short prompts (<=64 tokens) pfx hit went from ~78% down to ~21% on the canary fleet. overall tail latency up ~18%.
Dennis: which change correlates? kernel swap or quant bits?
Ajay: both landed in the same deploy. compiler changed kernel variant naming and the quant pipeline added a per-build salt for artifact ids. suspicion: cache key now includes variant id + salt -> misses.
Olivia: can you paste the keygen snippet from runtime?
Ajay: sure — before deploy we keyed on model_id + model_hash + prompt_hash. after deploy it became model_id + model_hash + kernel_variant + "-" + build_salt + prompt_hash, so salt is unstable between builds.
Ajay: snippet:
```
# simplified keygen (post-deploy)
key = f"{model_id}:{model_hash}:{kernel_variant}-{build_salt}:{prompt_prefix_hash}"
```
Leah: ugh. compiler added salt to identify microkernel builds, but we never intended it to affect prefix keying. we should canonicalize kernel_variant into a stable family id for keys.
Dennis: Agreed. Options: 1) strip build_salt when generating cache keys 2) map kernel_variant -> stable family tag 3) force fallback to previous kernel for pfx warmup workload.
Olivia: stripping salt seems lowest risk and fastest. can we prove no correctness regression? the salt shouldn't affect semantics, only artifact identity.
Ajay: confirmed on small repro: warmup workload with same prompt across two builds — different salts produced misses. When we remove salt from key the hits restore.
Leah: good. patch plan: runtime will normalize cache key by applying regex to kernel_variant to drop /salt-[0-9a-f]{6,}/ and map to stable name. add telemetry to monitor percent of keys normalized. PR target: runtime/main, will add unit + integration test.
Dennis: timeline? we should canary within 2 hours and revert if hit-rate doesn't recover.
Leah: I can do PR now. pinging runtime-ci for a quick run.
Leah: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9087 (WIP) — adds KernelKey.canonicalize and a feature flag `runtime.pfx_canonicalize_kernel` default on for canary.
runtime-ci: CI started for PR 9087 — tests: unit/integration/bench-warmup.
Ajay: for canary config, set feature on for 10% of served GPUs in us-west-2 canary cluster. measure 30m windows.
Olivia: add alert if pfx hit < 60% or p99 latency increases > 10% vs baseline.
Leah: pushed tests. excerpt from new test:
```
def test_kernel_key_canonicalize():
  k1 = "fused-attn-v4-salt-abc123"
  k2 = "fused-attn-v4-salt-def456"
  assert canonicalize(k1) == canonicalize(k2)
```
Leah: PR ready for review. @Dennis can you eyeball quick?
Dennis: reviewing now. quick suggestion: also log original kernel_variant in debug for a week to help audits.
Leah: will add.
deploy-bot: rolling canary deploy for runtime/main@pr-9087 to cluster canary-usw2 (10% nodes). estimated finish 00:07:12.
Ajay: starting synthetic warmup runner against canary with the typical short prompt mix.
Ajay: after 15m: pfx hit for canary restored to ~75%. baseline nodes still at 22%.
Olivia: nice. watch for eviction churn — if normalized keys cause longer-lived entries we might need to bump cache size or eviction thresholds.
Ajay: memory stable so far, eviction rate unchanged.
Dennis: hold on rollout until we have 1h of stability and no error spike >0.05%.
Leah: adding telemetry: `pfx_key_normalized_pct` and `pfx_hit_by_build` dashboard panel.
runtime-ci: canary tests passed. bench warmup shows steady-state cost down 12% on canary.
Ajay: after 1h: canary pfx hit 76% sustained, p99 latency down 15% vs pre-fix canary. no error spike.
Olivia: go for full rollout with gradual ramp. make sure to include log-based metrics for next 24h.
Dennis: rolling to 50% now. keep monitoring.
Leah: note for postmortem: root cause = artifact-level build_salt leaked into cache-key surface. mitigation = key canonicalization + compiler follow-up to not expose salt in variant string for runtime consumers.
Ajay: can we also backfill a migration that maps recent salts to stable families so old cached entries can be reused?
Leah: good idea — we can add a short-lived migration that takes metadata from artifact registry and writes normalized-key entries pointing to existing cached binaries. will scope as follow-up.
Olivia: thanks team. nice rapid detection + revertless fix. :tada: 
Leah: PR merged and fully rolled out by 1938642960. leaving this thread open for migration follow-up.
Ajay: filing ticket for artifact-registry migration: INF-2142.
Dennis: closing loop — great catch and quick fix. :pray:
